_README: Operational meaning of the tbl_use_case_ext.rule_text operators, and which source wins when
CONFIRMED by the business owner, relayed 2026-07-27. Before this, every operator was
'unconfirmed' and retriever/rule_text.py interpret() deliberately refused to guess.
'meaning' must be a value the interpreter actually implements (see _MEANINGS in
retriever/rule_text.py). An unrecognised meaning keeps interpretation switched OFF rather than
silently producing the wrong shape — so renaming a meaning here is safe, it fails closed.
CLOSED 2026-08-05: the follow-up on '>' is answered. 左边失败了才发 — the right side fires ONLY
when the left side fails, so stage_transition is 'fallback_on_failure'. This is the answer that
outage questions turn on: 'the LETTER vendor is down — do EMAIL and SMS still go out?' is now
'yes, that is exactly when they go out', not 'unconfirmed'. Note the inverse also becomes
sayable and matters more for blast radius: while the left channel is HEALTHY the right-hand
channels are NOT sending, so they must not be counted as live traffic.

>.note: 哪个大就哪个先发 — the left operand sends first; stages run left to right.

&.note: 一起发 — every channel in the group is sent together.

|.note: 二选一 — exactly one of the operands is used.

stage_transition_note: 左边失败了才发 — a '>' stage fires only when the preceding stage FAILED. Owner-confirmed 2026-08-05. Must be one of the values retriever/rule_text.py implements (_STAGE_TRANSITIONS); anything else falls back to 'unconfirmed' rather than being interpreted.

note: 以 rule_text 为准,没有的情况下再看 priority — rule_text is authoritative; the
tbl_use_case_channel_rule.priority column is the fallback used only when rule_text is
blank/absent. A disagreement is therefore still WORTH REPORTING as a data-quality issue,
but it is no longer an open question about which side is correct.

confirmed_by: business owner (relayed by the project owner)
